title: [Epic line] MCP write (MCP 写数): changing business records, running actions and moving approvals over the open MCP door
body:
epic:#34659#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnXJdSZifpEN5i7aU

Filing gate: ④ a coordination node under the cross-lane parent #34659 (the 「MCP 二期与问数」 epic), filed on the maintainer's word in this session's chat, 2026-11-18, verbatim: 「立 MCP写数 专题」. On why, verbatim: 「这个非常关键」. The name 「MCP 写数」 is the maintainer's.

## What this is

The line for an assistant that does things to business data over the open MCP door, as the pair of MCP ask (#35150): ask reads, write changes.

The tools exist on both doors today (`create_record`, `update_record`, `delete_record`, `run_action` and their kin). This line was in no parent: the ask line is read-only, and the build line changes metadata through drafts, not records.

## Scope

Three kinds of request, all in scope:

- Creating, changing and deleting records.
- Running an action (the thing behind a button).
- Moving a process: submitting for approval, approving, rejecting.

"Write" names the line; it is not limited to writing one row.

## Questions the line answers

- Before a write: when the user's confirmation is owed, and how a bulk change or a delete is bounded.
- On a refusal by permission or validation: the result names what refused and why, so the assistant can say it.
- Values: a select field takes its option value, not its label; how a related record is named.
- After a write: what the result shows was changed, and whether it can be taken back.

## What does not belong here

- Reading and answering: #35150 and its base #35159.
- Changing metadata: #35152 and its base #35160.
- The hosted product agent's own write path: hosted, linked later, not started.

## Order

**Second**, after MCP ask and ahead of MCP build. The maintainer, 2026-11-18, verbatim: 「把"写数"排第二，在问数之后、MCP 搭建之前。」

## Children

None yet, on purpose. A measurement round comes first: a set of real write tasks run against a local open-source server, scored on where they go wrong. Cards are filed from what it finds, with a shared base split out if hosted write turns out to wait on it.
